name: sph-ico-half
comment: HALF THE ICOSAHEDRON'S FACE. The icosahedron cuts the sphere into twenty equilateral triangles with 72-degree corners, because five faces meet at every vertex; an altitude cuts one into two 36-90-72 triangles. This is the first SCALENE half in the family, and so the first CHIRAL one: its three angles differ, its three sides differ, and its mirror image is a separate alphabet symbol — which is exactly the case the sided-classes repair of 2026-08-13 made runnable. The sides are the icosahedron's edge arccos(1/sqrt5) = 63.4349, half of it 31.7175, and the altitude 58.2825 degrees, so three edge types, none of them a round number. D=20 because 36 = 2pi/20 x 2; the angles are [2,5,4] and sum to 11 against the 10 a flat triangle would, so the excess is 1 unit = 18 degrees = pi/10 and every tiling uses exactly 4pi/(pi/10) = 40 tiles — the icosahedron's twenty faces, halved.
